ChenXinBest/hosts_check.description: Resolve tmdb hosts to prevent DNS pollution
ChenXinBest/hosts_check.body:
# hosts_check

Resolves available IPs for TMDB / GitHub domain names, generates `hosts.txt`, and bypasses DNS pollution. Supports IPv4 (A) and IPv6 (AAAA) records.

## Usage

- **Use the hosts file directly**: copy the [HOST daily update](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChenXinBest/hosts_check/master/hosts.txt) into your hosts file
- **Run manually**:
  ```bash
  pip install -r requirements.txt
  python -m dnsprobe
  ```
  Or install the package and run directly:
  ```bash
  pip install -e .
  dnsprobe
  ```

## Configuration

- `config.yml`: which providers to enable, each provider's upstream DNS, and output and reachability parameters
- `domains.yml`: the list of domain names to resolve

Edit `domains.yml` to customize your own domain list.

### IPv6 Support

Configure `record_types` in the provider's `extra` section in `config.yml`:

```yaml
providers:
  - name: doh
    extra:
      record_types: ["A"]          # IPv4 only (default)
      # record_types: ["AAAA"]     # IPv6 only
      # record_types: ["A", "AAAA"] # dual stack
```

## Adding a Custom Provider

Create a new `.py` file in the `plugins/` directory, inherit from `BaseResolver`, and decorate the class with `@register("name")`:

```python
from dnsprobe.registry import register
from dnsprobe.resolver import BaseResolver, ResolverConfig, ResolverError

@register("my_resolver")
class MyResolver(BaseResolver):
    def resolve(self, domain: str, cfg: ResolverConfig) -> list[str]:
        # cfg.upstream_dns: list[str] — list of upstream DNS servers (only meaningful for providers that support multiple upstream DNS servers)
        # cfg.extra: dict — …

## What is this

> 💬 **One-sentence version**: When you join, it helps you figure out the business and write it down in files. After you leave, every time your digital employee changes code or files, each change is checked against those files, logged, and snapshotted, so problems can be investigated and rolled back.

> The bottleneck for AI adoption has shifted from “is the model smart enough” to “will the organization dare to adopt it”: whether it can join the org chart, whether it has an account, how performance is measured, and how mistakes can be reversed. sofagent is the onboarding system for digital employees. On entry, it writes job responsibilities into files. On departure, it evaluates performance against those files (each change leaves evidence), keeps organizational memory (the accumulation mechanism iterates with use; for boundaries see [LIMITATIONS](https://github.com/KongFangXun/sofagent/blob/HEAD/docs/LIMITATIONS.md)), and tolerates trial and error (mistakes can be reversed). Before you give an AI a badge number, install sofagent first.

> sofagent is a **FDE deliverables governance layer with a built-in Harness**. The engineering layer (FDEing) and the governance layer (harness) have shipped; the judgment layer (S1M, the decision model that separates judgment from generation) is scheduled for construction in v1.6.0–v1.9.0 and declared at v2.0.0. The three layers each do their own job and do not substitute for one another.
> The identity formula is finalized as **FDEing × S1A (S1A = S1M + Harness)**. The source of truth for this wording = [PHILOSOPHY · identity wording](https://github.com/KongFangXun/sofagent/blob/HEAD/docs/PHILOSOPHY.md).

**Open-source FDE Harness layer** (Harness = “reins”, the governance layer that restrains the Agent; FDE = Forward Deployed Engineer, see “What is FDE Harness” below). It is embedded between mature Agents (DSH / OpenClaw / WorkBuddy) and the model layer to provide governance: on entry, business judgment is written into files (workflows / ontology data / AI nodes), and after departure each change is audited against those files. The constraint layer has five capabilities (injection, auditing, rollback, accumulation, evolution), distributed in five forms (FDE plugin / Skill / MCP / CLI / Dashboard).

ZaiZheTingDun/mash-app.body:
# Mash

An automation tool for Fate/Grand Order built with Tauri, Rust, and React. It connects to Android devices or emulators via ADB and performs actions using image recognition.

[Download and install](https://docs.mash.xiaotongx.com/start/install/) · [Usage docs](https://docs.mash.xiaotongx.com/) · [Development docs](https://github.com/ZaiZheTingDun/mash-app/blob/HEAD/docs/README.md) · [Contributing](https://github.com/ZaiZheTingDun/mash-app/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md)

## Features

- Auto battle: cast skills, use Noble Phantasms, and select command cards based on turn, battle phase, and custom conditions.
- Teams and support: manage Servant and Craft Essence configurations, and filter support Servants by conditions.
- Auto enhancement: Servant enhancement, Concept Craft Essence enhancement, and orb rolling (搓丸子).
- Friend Point summoning: automatically performs Friend Point draws.

## Installation and usage

Supports Windows x64 and macOS Apple Silicon. Go to the [installation guide](https://docs.mash.xiaotongx.com/start/install/) to download the version for your platform.

1. Start your Android device or emulator, enable the ADB connection, and run FGO.
2. In Mash, connect to the device, then install the CV runtime and resources as prompted.
3. Configure your teams and automation tasks, then start running.

## Local development

Requires Node.js 22, Rust stable, the pnpm version specified in `package.json`, and the Tauri build dependencies for your current platform. For environment setup and testing, see the [contributing guide](https://github.com/ZaiZheTingDun/mash-app/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ZaiZheTingDun/mash-app.git
cd mash-app
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm tauri dev
```

To preview only the frontend, run `pnpm dev`. Device connection and automation require the Tauri backend and an installed CV runtime.

## Project structure

```text
src/                  React UI
src-tauri/            Rust backend, automation engine, and app resources
sidecar/cv-code/      Python image recognition and video stream processing bundled with the app
sidecar/cv-runtime/   Native dependencies, OCR models, launcher, and standalone…
```

hloolx/codpl.body:
# CODPL

CODPL is a static evaluation site for multi-vendor Coding Plan / Code API services. It is used for Coding Plan evaluation, Coding Plan speed testing, Code API benchmarking, multi-vendor model comparison, and long-term trend tracking. The project continuously displays TTFT, MedianTPS, composite experience scores, and historical snapshots for different platforms and models, so developers can review real probe results before integration, procurement, and selection.

If you are searching for any of the following, this project is for you:

- Coding Plan evaluation
- Coding Plan benchmark
- Coding Plan speed test
- Coding Plan vendor comparison
- Coding Plan purchase reference
- Code API response speed comparison
- TTFT / MedianTPS / composite experience ranking

## Online Addresses

- Main site: <https://codpl.15o.cc>
- Overseas node: <https://bench.codpl.com/>
- Vendor onboarding status, purchase links, and official documentation entry points: <https://bench.codpl.com/providers>

The overseas node is served by Cloudflare and is suitable for access from outside China.

## What the Project Does

- Continuously probes multiple Coding Plan / Code API vendors and publicly displays the latest round of results.
- Compares time to first token (TTFT), MedianTPS, composite scores, and the performance of the same model across vendors.
- Accumulates historical data through static JSON snapshots, for observing 24-hour and 30-day trend changes.
- Provides developers, team procurement, and model selection with a public, intuitive, and verifiable reference page.

This repository is the frontend release repository. It keeps only the frontend code and snapshot data required by the static site, and does not include backend source code, databases, or private environment variables.

## Vendors Currently Covered by Probing

The public page currently covers the following Coding Plan / Code API vendors. For the full model list, see [BENCHMARK_COVERAGE.md](https://github.com/hloolx/codpl/blob/HEAD/BENCHMARK_COVERAGE.md):

# Open Guji CV

OCR analysis toolkit for ancient book images: character-by-character recognition, layout detection, and character grid localization on scanned images of ancient books.

---

## Overview

- **Automatic layout analysis**: automatically recognizes typesetting features of ancient books (border type, number of rows and columns, 筒子页/半页 (tongzi page / half page), spine shadow, etc.)
- **Step-by-step preprocessing**: crop spine → crop border → line enhancement → skew correction → split half pages → binarization
- **Layout detection**: detects borders (double / single layer) and column structure, outputs annotated visualization images
- **Character grid detection**: locates the bounding box of each character column by column, outputs structured JSON
- **OCR recognition**: based on PaddleOCR, supports both CPU and GPU modes
- **Table recognition**: for table pages in ancient books, extracts row and column structure and cell text

---

## Installation

### Prerequisites

- Python 3.10+
- (Optional) CUDA 12.x + NVIDIA GPU (measured on RTX 3080: about 1.5 seconds per page)

### 1. Clone the repository and create a virtual environment

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/open-guji-cv.git
cd open-guji-cv
python -m venv venv
```

### 2a. CPU mode installation

```bash
venv/Scripts/pip install -e ".[cpu]"   # Windows
# or
venv/bin/pip install -e ".[cpu]"        # Linux/macOS
```

### 2b. GPU mode installation (recommended, about 7-8x faster)

**Windows:**
```bat
install_gpu.bat
```

**Linux:**
```bash
bash install_gpu.sh
```

Or manually:
```bash
# Install GPU version of PaddlePaddle (for CUDA 12.x)
pip install paddlepaddle-gpu -i https://www.paddlepaddle.org.cn/packages/stable/cu123/
pip install -e ".[gpu]"
```

### 3. Set environment variables (recommended)

```bash
export PADDLE_PDX_DISABLE_MODEL_SOURCE_CHECK=True   # Skip model source connectivity check to speed up startup
export PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8                         # Required for Chinese output in Windows console
```

---

## Quick Start

```bash
# Step 1: Analyze layout features

sqing33/docker-image-sync.body:
# 🚀 Docker Image Toolbox: Build and Sync

This project is a collection of GitHub Actions workflows, designed to provide a one-stop Docker image management solution.

It mainly includes two core features:

1. **Building multi-architecture images from Git repositories**: Pull the source code of any Git repository, automatically build Docker images supporting multiple CPU architectures (such as `amd64`, `arm64`), and push them to Docker Hub and GitHub Packages (`ghcr.io`).
2. **Syncing public images to speed up downloads**: Sync images from public registries such as Docker Hub to your own `ghcr.io` repository to speed up image pulls in mainland China and other regions. If `ghcr.io` is still not fast enough, it can be used together with the Nanjing University acceleration station `ghcr.nju.edu.cn`.

## ✨ Key Features

- **Dual core**: Combines image **building** and **syncing** in one, meeting needs in different scenarios.
- **Manual trigger**: All workflows can be started manually from the Actions page via a simple form.
- **Multi-architecture support**: Easily build images for `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`, `linux/arm/v7`, and other CPU architectures.
- **Multi-registry push**: Build once and automatically push images to GitHub Packages (`ghcr.io`) and Docker Hub.
- **Automatic updates**: Synced images get a daily automatic update mechanism, ensuring the version you use is always up to date.
- **Automated results**: After a workflow runs successfully, the image list in this `README.md` file is automatically updated.
- **Secure and reliable**: Manage your private credentials securely through GitHub's encrypted Secrets, avoiding hardcoding risks.

## 🛠️ First-time Installation and Configuration

For all features to work properly, the safest and most recommended approach is to **Fork this project** to your own GitHub account, then complete the following one-time configuration.

### Step 1: Fork this project

🍴 Click the **"Fork"** button in the upper right corner of this project page to copy this repository to your own account. All subsequent operations will be performed in your forked repository.

### Step 2: Configure repository permissions

🔐 This is the key to allowing Actions to automatically modify `README.md` and manage images.

1. On your forked repository page, click **"Settings"** -> **"Actions"** -> **"General"**.
